You embed with an enterprise team, find the work that actually warrants AI, architect the system, build it, and stay long enough to make it survive contact with production. This is a three-way role: consultant, operator, engineer. You should be as comfortable pressure-testing a business case with a COO or VP of Engineering as you are diagnosing why retrieval quality collapsed after a data refresh. The people who succeed here can hold a discovery conversation on Monday and ship what they scoped on Thursday. On this track, your edge is data, retrieval, and model behavior: you make agents trustworthy by getting the data, context, and evaluation right. We work with regulated industries and Fortune 500 clients who have AI mandates, real constraints, and low tolerance for demos that don’t hold up. How We Approach The Work FDEs are trusted to shape the solution, not only deliver it. Every engagement calls for architect-level judgment: Reframes the request. Treats “we need an agent for X” as a hypothesis, not a spec. Decomposes the problem. Outcome → process → decisions → data → systems → actors → constraints — before choosing technology. Chooses the intervention. Remove, simplify, traditional software, automation, LLM, RAG, agent, or multi-agent — and defends why. Owns the architecture decision. Documents trade-offs (ADRs), sets success metrics, pushes back on scope that won’t deliver value. Consultative Discovery Clients rarely arrive with a fully formed problem, and the FDE’s first contribution is helping them see it clearly. You lead discovery with genuine curiosity, moving the conversation from stated requirements to underlying needs, and you build credibility through the depth of your understanding rather than the breadth of your pitch. Uncovers business drivers. What outcome matters, what it’s worth, why now, and what happens if nothing changes. Uncovers personal drivers. What each stakeholder is measured on, what they’re worried about, and what a win looks like for them individually. Surfaces constraints early. Security, compliance, data access, budget, skills, politics, timelines — the things that kill projects in month two. Aligns stakeholders. Spots conflicting goals between business, engineering, and risk, and brings them to a shared definition of success. Asks strategic questions. Follows the answer with “why,” “how do you know,” and “what happens today when…” — without interrogating. Clients leave the conversation understanding their own problem better. Earns authority through depth. Credibility comes from the quality of the questions and the insight in the playback, not from pitching technology. What You'll Do Discover. Run workshops and process discovery with business, data, and engineering stakeholders. Assess data readiness honestly. Separate genuine AI problems from workflow problems wearing an AI costume. Structure the process and the spec. For any business process being automated, map the current state, decision points, data inputs, and exceptions, then turn it into specifications that both people and AI systems can execute against reliably. Architect & design. Design agentic systems end to end with emphasis on context and retrieval architecture — data sourcing, chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, permissions-aware retrieval, knowledge graphs where warranted — plus orchestration, MCP/tool integration, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Build. Ship working systems — agents, retrieval services, evaluation tooling, and the data flows that feed them. Prototypes that prove value in weeks, not slideware. Engineer the delivery system. Own CI/CD for what you build, extended to AI: prompt and context versioning, eval suites that run in the pipeline and gate releases. Operate (Day 2). Own what happens after launch — eval harnesses, groundedness and retrieval metrics, observability and tracing, cost and latency management, drift, and the handoff that lets the client’s team run it without you. Consult. Present to and defend decisions in front of CTOs, VPs of Engineering, CDOs, and business leadership. Quantify impact in their terms. Support pre-sales scoping and proposal work when the deal calls for it. Hands-on experience with frontier AI developer tools including Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or OpenAI Codex. Track record of leading client-facing discovery calls, asking "why" before "how" to decompose unstructured business problems. Solid understanding of architecture paradigms such as RESTful APIs, microservices, and event-driven systems. Well-versed in agentic orchestration tools and frameworks like LangGraph, LangChain, N8N, or direct Model Context Protocol (MCP) and LLM APIs. Skilled at exercising end-to-end delivery ownership and managing project scope without requiring product manager supervision. Ability to work through new and difficult issues and contribute to libraries as needed. Ability to create and maintain continuous integration and delivery of applications. Forensic attention to detail. A positive mindset and a can-do attitude. Experience working on Agile / Scrum teams. Meaningful experience working on large, complex systems. We're looking for a Business Analyst to turn business problems into clear, buildable requirements. You'll sit between our clients, our product team, and our engineers: running discovery, mapping processes, writing user stories and acceptance criteria, and making sure what we ship actually solves the problem it was meant to solve. You'll work across a mix of client builds, client maintenance engagements, and Bluelight's internal products, and you'll play a key role when new projects are being scoped and estimated. Responsibilities Lead stakeholder interviews and workshops with clients and internal teams to understand goals, current workflows, and pain points. Document current-state and future-state processes, business rules, data definitions, and edge cases. Support new-project sizing by breaking scope into epics and stories that engineering can estimate with confidence. Identify assumptions, risks, dependencies, and open questions early, and drive them to resolution. Write clear user stories with testable acceptance criteria in Jira. Partner with the Product Manager to prioritize and groom the backlog ahead of each two-week sprint. Work with UI/UX design in Figma to make sure flows and screens match the requirements, and flag gaps before development starts. Answer engineering questions during the sprint and keep requirements current as decisions are made. Work with QA to make sure acceptance criteria translate into solid test coverage. Support sprint demos and coordinate user acceptance testing with clients. Keep requirements documentation organized in Google Drive so decisions and their rationale are easy to find later. Make sure compliance, security, and audit requirements (including SOC 2 considerations) are captured as explicit requirements, not afterthoughts. Act as a trusted point of contact for clients on scope and requirements questions. Translate between business and technical audiences clearly and without jargon in either direction. Surface scope changes early and help the team and client understand the tradeoffs. Requirements 3+ years as a Business Analyst, Product Analyst, or similar role on software projects. Strong experience writing user stories and acceptance criteria in an agile/Scrum environment. Proven ability to run discovery sessions and turn ambiguous input into structured requirements. Comfort with process mapping and data modeling at a business level (flows, entities, relationships, rules). Hands-on experience with Jira; familiarity with Figma and collaborative docs. Excellent written and spoken English; comfortable leading client meetings with U.S. stakeholders. Enough technical literacy to have productive conversations with engineers about APIs, integrations, databases, and system constraints. Nice to Have Experience in an agency, consultancy, or software services environment juggling multiple clients. Exposure to regulated or compliance-heavy domains (e.g., SOC 2, telecom/outbound compliance, education, fintech). Experience writing requirements for integrations with third-party platforms. Familiarity with web application stacks (e.g., Laravel, React) and AWS. Experience supporting estimation or proposal work for new projects. Company Benefits Competitive salary and bonuses, including performance-based salary increases. Generous paid-time-off policy Flexible working hours Work remotely Continuing education, training, conferences Company-sponsored coursework, exams, and certifications Being a consultant in our team is a fun, challenging, and rewarding career choice. Your contributions are highly valued by clients, and the work you do often has a direct and significant impact on their business. You will have the opportunity to work on a variety of projects for our incredible clients, which will accelerate your career growth. You’ll collaborate with modern technologies and work alongside some of the best professionals in the industry! We're looking for a Business Analyst to turn business problems into clear, buildable requirements. You'll sit between our clients, our product team, and our engineers: running discovery, mapping processes, writing user stories and acceptance criteria, and making sure what we ship actually solves the problem it was meant to solve. You'll work across a mix of client builds, client maintenance engagements, and Bluelight's internal products, and you'll play a key role when new projects are being scoped and estimated. Responsibilities Lead stakeholder interviews and workshops with clients and internal teams to understand goals, current workflows, and pain points. Document current-state and future-state processes, business rules, data definitions, and edge cases. Support new-project sizing by breaking scope into epics and stories that engineering can estimate with confidence. Identify assumptions, risks, dependencies, and open questions early, and drive them to resolution. Write clear user stories with testable acceptance criteria in Jira. Partner with the Product Manager to prioritize and groom the backlog ahead of each two-week sprint. Work with UI/UX design in Figma to make sure flows and screens match the requirements, and flag gaps before development starts. Answer engineering questions during the sprint and keep requirements current as decisions are made. Work with QA to make sure acceptance criteria translate into solid test coverage. Support sprint demos and coordinate user acceptance testing with clients. Keep requirements documentation organized in Google Drive so decisions and their rationale are easy to find later. Make sure compliance, security, and audit requirements (including SOC 2 considerations) are captured as explicit requirements, not afterthoughts. Act as a trusted point of contact for clients on scope and requirements questions. Translate between business and technical audiences clearly and without jargon in either direction. Surface scope changes early and help the team and client understand the tradeoffs. Requirements 3+ years as a Business Analyst, Product Analyst, or similar role on software projects. Strong experience writing user stories and acceptance criteria in an agile/Scrum environment. Proven ability to run discovery sessions and turn ambiguous input into structured requirements. Comfort with process mapping and data modeling at a business level (flows, entities, relationships, rules). Hands-on experience with Jira; familiarity with Figma and collaborative docs. Excellent written and spoken English; comfortable leading client meetings with U.S. stakeholders. Enough technical literacy to have productive conversations with engineers about APIs, integrations, databases, and system constraints. Nice to Have Experience in an agency, consultancy, or software services environment juggling multiple clients. Exposure to regulated or compliance-heavy domains (e.g., SOC 2, telecom/outbound compliance, education, fintech). Experience writing requirements for integrations with third-party platforms. Familiarity with web application stacks (e.g., Laravel, React) and AWS. Experience supporting estimation or proposal work for new projects. Company Benefits Competitive salary and bonuses, including performance-based salary increases. Generous paid-time-off policy Flexible working hours Work remotely Continuing education, training, conferences Company-sponsored coursework, exams, and certifications Being a consultant in our team is a fun, challenging, and rewarding career choice. Your contributions are highly valued by clients, and the work you do often has a direct and significant impact on their business. You will have the opportunity to work on a variety of projects for our incredible clients, which will accelerate your career growth. You’ll collaborate with modern technologies and work alongside some of the best professionals in the industry! Client Accounting & Advisory Services Location: Argentina Work Arrangement: Remote Employment Type: Full-Time, Independent Contractor Compensation: Up to USD 4,000/month Work Schedule: Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm EST About Convoy Finance We like working with people who move fast, think for themselves, and care about doing great work. That's pretty much how we run Convoy. We're a small finance and accounting firm working with technology, SaaS, fintech and Web3 companies across Canada and internationally. Our clients are ambitious businesses, and we work directly with the founders and finance teams building them. That means we're not just looking at numbers all day. We get to see what's happening inside growing companies and help the people running them make better decisions. One week you might be leading a month-end close, and the next you could be helping a client work through a reporting issue, improve their financial processes or solve something completely new. We're a small team, too. Most of us are based in Toronto, with a few people working remotely around the world. There's very little bureaucracy, decisions happen quickly, and good ideas can actually turn into action. The Opportunity We're looking for an Accounting Manager who can take ownership, think beyond the books and be a trusted partner to our clients. You'll oversee accounting work across a portfolio of growing companies and work directly with international clients, founders, CFOs and senior finance professionals . You'll be responsible for making sure the accounting is accurate, the work gets done well and client deliverables stay on track. But we also expect you to look beyond the numbers: understand what's happening in the business, identify issues before they become problems and bring ideas to the table. This is a hands-on management role. You'll still be close to the accounting, while also reviewing work, guiding team members, managing priorities and helping clients navigate more complex accounting and finance questions. Our clients move quickly, and so do we. There will be deadlines, competing priorities and new problems to solve. We're looking for someone who is comfortable operating with a high degree of independence and can make good decisions without needing everything mapped out for them. As an Accounting Manager, you'll have significant ownership over your client relationships and the opportunity to grow into broader advisory, financial management and leadership responsibilities . What You'll Do You'll take ownership of: Managing a portfolio of client accounts, ensuring accurate and timely delivery of accounting and reporting work Leading and overseeing full-cycle accounting and month-end close, including reconciliations, journal entries, AP/AR and financial statement preparation Reviewing accounting work and ensuring quality, accuracy and consistency across client deliverables Preparing and reviewing financial statements, management reports and financial analysis Working directly with founders, CFOs and senior finance teams to answer questions, resolve issues and provide accounting guidance Managing client deadlines, priorities and deliverables, and proactively communicating when something needs attention Supporting year-end compilations, audits, reviews and tax-related work Identifying opportunities to improve accounting processes, systems and controls Coaching and supporting more junior members of the accounting team Taking ownership of more complex accounting issues and helping the team determine the right approach Supporting advisory and finance projects as they come up Building strong, long-term relationships with clients and becoming a trusted point of contact for their accounting needs Requirements What We're Looking For You have a Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field and 5+ years of relevant accounting experience , with significant experience in a client-facing accounting, public accounting, audit or advisory environment. Big Four experience is required for this role. We're looking for someone who has been exposed to high standards of quality, complex accounting work and demanding client environments, and who is ready to take that experience into a more hands-on, ownership-driven role. You're confident owning full-cycle accounting, month-end close and financial reporting , while also reviewing work, managing priorities and ensuring that client deliverables are accurate and delivered on time. You're comfortable working directly with clients, founders, CFOs and senior finance professionals . You communicate clearly in English and can explain what the numbers mean — not just what the numbers are. This role is 100% in English , both internally and with clients. You're also someone who likes to figure things out . If something looks wrong, you investigate it. If you don't know the answer, you find it. If there's a better way to do something, you speak up. You're comfortable making decisions, taking ownership and working independently without needing every step spelled out. You have experience reviewing or mentoring other accountants and are comfortable providing guidance, giving feedback and taking responsibility for the quality of the work delivered by your team. Experience with QuickBooks Online, Xero, Taxprep or CaseWare is a plus, as is experience working with SaaS, technology, fintech or Web3 companies . A CPA designation or active CPA pursuit is also a plus. Benefits Why Convoy? You'll work with interesting companies, smart people and problems that don't always come with an instruction manual. You'll have direct exposure to founders and senior finance leaders and get to see how growing companies actually operate. Because we're small, your work is visible and your ideas can have an impact. We're remote-friendly, with team members working from Toronto and different parts of the world. We also make time for team lunches, happy hours and, when the numbers are good, the occasional team trip. It's fast-paced. It's challenging. And it's definitely not boring. If you want a role where you can keep learning, take real ownership and grow beyond traditional accounting , we'd like to hear from you. descripcion: Requirements Description & Requirements Resumen de trabajo El rol de líder clave es una parte esencial del equipo de liderazgo de la tienda, y afecta a los miembros del equipo de la planta de ventas y a la experiencia de los huéspedes (es decir, los clientes) todos los días. Los líderes clave son responsables de predicar con el ejemplo y brindar apoyo a los educadores, facilitar una excelente experiencia para los huéspedes en la tienda y supervisar todas las operaciones del piso minorista. Los líderes clave aprovechan los indicadores y métricas clave de desempeño para priorizar las responsabilidades mientras se adaptan a los ajustes y desafíos comerciales diarios. Responsabilidades clave del trabajo Liderazgo y Gestión de Personas Apoyar el aprendizaje y el desarrollo continuo de los miembros del equipo proporcionando retroalimentación directa, entrenamiento, tutoría y orientación profesional, y abordando inquietudes de desempeño. Proporcionar reconocimiento a los miembros del equipo, evaluación de brechas y documentación de desempeño general para respaldar y reforzar el crecimiento personal y profesional. Desarrollar, mantener y difundir el producto y el conocimiento general de la empresa a través de canales de comunicación adecuados. Experiencia del huésped (es decir, del cliente) Proporcionar liderazgo en el piso de ventas a los miembros del equipo, incluida la planificación de la cobertura del piso de ventas y la toma de decisiones para mantener la eficiencia y eficacia de las operaciones del piso de ventas. Apoyar a los miembros del equipo (p. ej., liderando con el ejemplo o brindando capacitación) para garantizar una excelente experiencia para los huéspedes que valore su tiempo, incluida la evaluación de las necesidades de los huéspedes, brindando educación técnica sobre productos y respaldando transacciones en la tienda y programas omnicanal (p. ej., compra en línea/ opciones de recogida en tienda, venta telefónica y envío desde tienda). Interactuar y evaluar las necesidades únicas de los huéspedes para brindarles soporte y soluciones de compra y devolución efectivas y personalizadas. Proporcionar educación técnica sobre el producto articulando el valor y beneficio del producto. Resolver los comentarios de los huéspedes y abordar sus inquietudes o derivaciones para que sean “correctos” para los huéspedes. Muévase dinámicamente en la sala para evaluar y satisfacer las necesidades del negocio, el equipo y los invitados. Trabajando con otros Contribuir a un ambiente de equipo respetuoso e inclusivo dando la bienvenida y celebrando las diferencias para garantizar una experiencia de apoyo y participación para todos los miembros del equipo e invitados. Establecer relaciones productivas y de apoyo con todos los miembros del equipo. Colaborar con los miembros del equipo para garantizar una experiencia óptima para los huéspedes y respaldar las operaciones de la tienda. Operaciones Revisar datos y métricas comerciales para evaluar el progreso hacia las metas y determinar si se justifican ajustes. Abrir y cerrar la tienda de acuerdo con las listas de verificación de apertura y cierre. Gestionar las tareas de presentación de productos (por ejemplo, volver a colocar los artículos en su lugar, reponer o agregar artículos agotados al piso desde el inventario, eliminar existencias o reubicar artículos) de acuerdo con los estándares de la empresa. Asigne a los educadores tareas de limpieza según sea necesario durante el turno para mantener el ambiente de lujo de la tienda. Garantizar que el equipo utilice la tecnología de la tienda para respaldar las operaciones de la tienda y brindar experiencias positivas a los huéspedes. Comprender y cumplir las políticas y procedimientos de seguridad de las personas para mantener un ambiente de trabajo seguro. Realizar el trabajo de acuerdo con las políticas, procedimientos y leyes o regulaciones aplicables. Responsabilidad presupuestaria No aplica Gestión de Personas Rol de líder del equipo, responsable indirectamente del subconjunto de empleados de la tienda en el piso o según lo delegado por el gerente de la tienda. Habilidades clave y valores fundamentales que aporta Inclusión y diversidad: crea/apoya un entorno inclusivo que valora/celebra las diferencias Integridad/Honestidad: Se comporta de manera honesta, justa y ética. Experiencia del huésped: disfruta trabajando y conectando, comprendiendo y ayudando a los huéspedes. Colaboración y trabajo en equipo: trabaja productivamente y apoya a otros para lograr sus objetivos; busca asociaciones y perspectivas diversas Liderazgo: es capaz y desea liderar, influir e inspirar a otros; Motiva, empodera, desarrolla y dirige a las personas mientras trabajan. Comunicación sincera: está dispuesto a compartir inquietudes de manera abierta y constructiva (es decir, hablar con franqueza) Toma de decisiones: utiliza la lógica y el razonamiento para evaluar alternativas y tomar decisiones efectivas y oportunas. Requisitos de trabajo Elegibilidad Debe estar legalmente autorizado para trabajar en el país en el que se encuentra la tienda. Debe tener 18 años de edad o más. Debe tener prueba del Derecho al Trabajo y evidencia relacionada con los requisitos legislativos locales asociados (solo EMEA) Debe tener la capacidad de viajar a la tienda asignada con métodos de transporte propios. Disponibilidad Dispuesto a trabajar en un horario flexible que incluya tardes, fines de semana y días festivos. Otros requisitos de voluntad Dispuesto a trabajar como parte de un equipo y también completar el trabajo de forma independiente. Estar dispuesto a moverse por una tienda durante la mayor parte del turno para ayudar a los huéspedes y realizar el trabajo. Dispuesto a mover cajas que pesen hasta 30 libras (13,6 kg) Dispuesto a trabajar en un ambiente con luces brillantes y música alta. Experiencia Experiencia laboral Activos laborales (es decir, es bueno tenerlos; no es obligatorio) Educación: diploma de escuela secundaria, GED o equivalente Educación: Licenciatura o equivalente Experiencia: 1 año de experiencia en liderazgo de ventas/venta minorista (no es necesario supervisor o gestión de personas) Job Summary The Key Leader role is an essential part of the store leadership team, impacting salesfloor team members and guest (i.e., customer) experience every day. Key Leaders are responsible for leading by example and providing support to Educators, facilitating an outstanding guest experience in the store, and overseeing all operations of the retail floor. Key Leaders leverage key performance indicators and metrics to prioritize responsibilities while adapting to day-to-day business adjustments and challenges. Key Responsibilities Of The Job Leadership and People Management Support ongoing learning and development of team members by providing direct feedback, coaching, mentoring, and career path guidance, and addressing performance concerns. Provide team members recognition, gap assessment, and overall performance documentation to support and reinforce career and personal growth. Develop, maintain, and disseminate product and general company knowledge through appropriate communication channels. Guest (i.e., Customer) Experience Provide salesfloor leadership to team members, including planning salesfloor coverage and making decisions to maintain efficiency and effectiveness of salesfloor operations. Support team members (e.g., leading by example or coaching) with ensuring a great guest experience that values guests’ time, including assessing guest needs, providing technical product educations, and supporting in-store transactions and omnichannel programs (e.g., buy online/pickup in store, phone sales, and ship from store options). Interact with and assess guests’ unique needs to provide customized, effective purchase and return solutions and support. Provide technical product education by articulating the value and benefit of the product. Resolve guest feedback and address guest concerns or escalations to make it “right” for guests. Move dynamically on the floor to assess and fulfill the needs of the business, team, and guests. Working With Others Contribute to a respectful and inclusive team environment by welcoming and celebrating differences to ensure a supportive and engaging experience for all team members and guests. Establish supportive and productive relationships with all team members. Collaborate with team members to ensure optimal guest experience and support store operations. Operations Review business data and metrics to evaluate progress toward goals and determine if adjustments are warranted. Open and close the store in accordance with the opening and closing checklists. Manage product presentation tasks (e.g., put items back in place, restock or add depleted items to the floor from inventory, destock or relocate items) according to company standards. Assign Educators cleaning tasks as needed throughout the shift to maintain the luxury environment of the store. Ensure team uses in-store technology to support store operations and provide positive guest experiences. Understand and adhere to people safety policies and procedures to maintain a safe work environment. Perform work in accordance with applicable policies, procedures, and laws or regulations. Budget Responsibility Not Applicable People Management Team lead role indirectly responsible for subset of store employees on the floor or as delegated by Store Manager Key Skills & Core Values You Bring Inclusion & Diversity: Creates/supports an inclusive environment that values/celebrates differences Integrity/Honesty: Behaves in an honest, fair, and ethical manner Guest Experience: Enjoys working and connecting with, understanding, and helping guests Collaboration and Teamwork: Works productively with and supports others to achieve goals; seeks partnerships and diverse perspectives Leadership: Is able and desires to lead, influence, and inspire others; motivates, empowers, develops, and directs people as they work Candid Communication: Is willing to openly/constructively share concerns (i.e., straight talk) Decision Making: Uses logic and reasoning to evaluate alternatives and make effective, timely decisions Job Requirements Eligibility Must be legally authorized to work in the country in which the store is located Must be 18 years of age or older Must have proof of the Right to Work and evidence relating to associated local legislative requirements (EMEA only) Must have the ability to travel to assigned store with own transportation methods Availability Willing to work a flexible schedule including evenings, weekends, and holidays Other Willingness Requirements Willing to work as part of a team and also complete work independently Willing to move through a store for most of a shift to help guests and accomplish work Willing to move boxes weighing up to 30 lbs (13.6 kg) Willing to work in an environment with bright lights and loud music Experience Work experience Job Assets (i.e., nice to have; not required) Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent Experience: 1 year of retail/sales leadership experience (supervisor or people management not necessary) Show more Show less

titulo: Email and SMS Marketing - Sports Sales Coordinator
descripcion: Turn interest into bookings—and keep players coming back Community Sports Partners operates sports and recreation businesses. We are looking for someone who combines strong email and SMS marketing skills with sales follow-through and organized day-to-day coordination. Your work will connect three things: campaigns that generate interest, conversations that turn interest into bookings, and pickup games that run smoothly enough for people to return. You will help sell available sports facility time and permit-backed bookings, support pickup-game operations remotely, and build email and SMS campaigns that increase participation and repeat business. What You Will Own Email and SMS marketing Plan, write, build and send campaigns promoting available facility time, pickup games, registration opportunities and relevant offers Create useful segments by location, sport, expressed interest, booking history and engagement Build and improve welcome messages, lead follow-up, incomplete-booking recovery where supported, reminders, repeat-booking and win-back flows Write clear English copy with specific offers and calls to action. Adapt existing brand assets into mobile-friendly emails Check audiences, dates, time zones, prices, links, personalization and suppression rules before launch Monitor delivery failures, bounces, complaints and opt-outs; maintain consent records and healthy lists Test messaging, timing, offers and journeys, then report qualified enquiries, paid bookings, repeat participation and revenue alongside engagement metrics Permit and facility-time sales Maintain an accurate view of available locations, dates, time slots, capacity and approved pricing Respond to enquiries from teams, coaches, leagues, organizers and other customers looking for sports space Understand what customers need, recommend suitable availability, prepare approved quotes and follow up through booking and payment confirmation Keep the sales pipeline current, document customer commitments and pursue renewals or repeat bookings Coordinate with the operations team before promising availability or exceptions. Escalate pricing, terms and conflicts outside your authority Pickup-game coordination Create and maintain accurate game listings, including location, start time, capacity, pricing and player instructions Monitor registrations and fill levels; use targeted outreach to help fill available places Coordinate with local hosts and venue contacts, making sure each game has the information and support it needs Manage routine player questions and waitlists, and communicate approved changes promptly Identify low-enrolment games, host gaps or venue problems early and escalate cancellation, refund or safety decisions to the appropriate manager Track attendance, feedback and repeat participation, and use what you learn to improve future games This is one role advertised across multiple recruitment locations. Applicants throughout Latin America are welcome. Please apply once using your preferred location listing. Requirements What we are looking for Practical experience building email campaigns and automations, plus hands-on SMS experience Strong written and spoken English for North American customer conversations Confidence following up with leads, explaining an offer and asking for the booking Strong attention to detail with schedules, prices, customer records and competing deadlines Experience with a CRM and an email/SMS platform; examples include Klaviyo, ActiveCampaign, HubSpot, Mailchimp or comparable tools. Experience with every platform is not required Comfort using spreadsheets and reports to understand conversion, bookings and campaign performance Dependable communication and willingness to own the next action until an issue is resolved Availability to work evenings and weekends in Toronto/Eastern time is required. This is when most games and customer activity take place, so these shifts are a core part of the role. The specific weekly schedule will be agreed before hiring Experience in sports, venue bookings, inside sales, event coordination, customer service or ecommerce retention is helpful. You should enjoy both campaign execution and customer follow-through. What Success Looks Like In the first month, learn the inventory, customer journeys and operating processes; audit existing campaigns and establish a reliable follow-up and QA routine. Over the following two months, take ownership of the campaign calendar and sales pipeline, improve priority automations, and make pickup-game coordination dependable. We will agree measurable goals for paid bookings, use of available facility time, game fill rates, repeat participation and service quality after reviewing the baseline. Apply with your resume and answer the questions in this application. Remove customer data and confidential employer information from examples. Applicants throughout Latin America are welcome; the selected location is a recruitment location, not a residence requirement. Required Assessments Please complete both standard assessments before or shortly after applying, using the same email address as your application. If you have already completed them for Community Sports Partners with that email, indicate this in the application. Culture Index survey Criteria GAME assessment — English Benefits Remote from Latin America. Monthly base of US$800-US$1,000 based on experience, plus expected variable commissions of US$500-US$1,000. Expected total US$1,300-US$2,000 per month. Commissions depend on performance and are not guaranteed. Evening and weekend work in Toronto/Eastern time is required, when most games and customer activity take place. The specific weekly schedule and commission terms will be agreed before hiring. Less rigidity, more flexibility, and technology and AI woven through how the work gets done — increasingly so, every quarter. Ejecutar el análisis exhaustivo de registros (logs) y telemetría en plataformas de observabilidad (como Datadog) para la identificación y diagnóstico preciso de anomalías, asegurando la detección temprana de incidentes que afecten la continuidad del servicio. Monitorear proactivamente la infraestructura y aplicaciones utilizando herramientas de APM, analizando fuentes de datos críticas para minimizar el tiempo medio de detección (MTTD) y proporcionar información clave para la remediación de fallas. Observabilidad y Confiabilidad Trabajar activamente con plataformas de observabilidad para analizar dashboards, interpretar alertas y detectar patrones anómalos o desvíos respecto al comportamiento esperado. Colaborar en la mejora continua de indicadores operativos, definición de umbrales y construcción de vistas que traduzcan métricas técnicas en impacto de negocio. Anticipación y Gestión Preventiva Identificar señales tempranas de picos de carga, degradación de performance o riesgo de saturación de capacidad. Elevar alertas preventivas y proponer acciones antes de que se materialicen incidentes, especialmente en jornadas de alta sensibilidad operativa. Contexto de Mercado Comprender la dinámica del mercado financiero y sus eventos relevantes (aperturas, cierres, vencimientos, jornadas de alta volatilidad), correlacionando dichos eventos con el comportamiento técnico de las plataformas. Mejora Continua y aspecto clave del perfil Participar en análisis post-incidente (post-mortems), documentar aprendizajes y contribuir a la construcción progresiva de prácticas de confiabilidad dentro del área de Operaciones. descripcion: A little about us: The Red Alpha Data Science practice grew out of Red Alpha's reputation in Software and System Engineering with our Department of Defense clients. As sometimes happens, customers who trust our expertise in adjacent areas asked Red Alpha to assist with some of their burgeoning Data Science problems. Culturally, it probably suffices to say that we take our work seriously, but not ourselves. Our leaders have spent time in the trenches and have cursed daylight savings time changes and trailing whitespace as many times as you have. We like to say that we spend 80% of our time cleaning the data...and 20% of our time complaining about cleaning the data. Joking aside, our voices matter, and it is easy to see how our decisions affect the Data Science practice and Red Alpha as a whole. We have a clear vision of where we are headed. Our team takes a pragmatic approach to Data Science, defining it loosely as the intersection of technical expertise, business acumen, and soft skills to solve business problems with data. We spend a lot of time trying to understand the problem before we set about building a solution, and we prefer lower tech useful solutions over shiny algorithms and dust on the shelf. Did we mention we’re pragmatic? We have a diverse set of skills across our team, and whether you are a traditional Data Scientist (whatever that means…), an Applied Research Mathematician, a Database Engineer, a Full Stack Developer, or something else in that neighborhood, if you have a knack for picking apart data to make sense of it, we would enjoy having a conversation with you. A day in the life: You’ll likely start your day at a customer location near our Red Alpha offices, checking to see if there are any important items that have just come up. If not, you’ll move on to improving a dashboard or other data product that you’re responsible for, or perhaps produce a weekly output the customer is expecting. You’ll be using R or Python a lot, but also Git, Mongo, some commercial software and several other usual suspects. Once a week you’ll attend a team meeting (with 4 others) to prioritize things, and you’ll have a lot of interaction with the team otherwise, typically several times per day. You’ll need your sense of humor and need to be willing to leave your ego at the door. What you bring to the table: Now on to the fun of formal requirements - we have to apologize in advance for the corporate-speak here, but just hold your breath for a few lines and everything will be okay. We are actively hiring data professionals for roles across a broad range of skill levels and projects. Our goal is to find the best fit for you so please note that if you apply to one of them and we see a fit elsewhere we will let you know. So do not worry about applying initially for every position you might be interested in. All of our data scientists need the following skills: Proficiency with a scripting language such as R or Python Experience with data science techniques and algorithms such as classification, clustering, random forests, deterministic forests (jk), hierarchical modeling, deep learning, Markov Chain Monte Carlo, and others. Note that you do not need to have all of these (we hope you enjoyed our random smattering of techniques…!) but you should be comfortable and capable with several of them and know some others not on this list. A B.S. Degree in Data Science, Mathematics, Computer Science or related field. For entry-level data scientists, 0-3 years of experience on Data Science projects. For mid-level data scientists, 3-6 years of experience on Data Science projects. For senior-level data scientists, at least 6 years of experience on Data Science projects with at least 3 years of experience managing teams. A TS/SCI with Polygraph security clearance. These are important skills to have, but not necessarily mandatory: Exceptional interpersonal skills. You know, as in you might not be at the top of the list to be a game show host but you do like people and enjoy solving problems jointly with your colleagues. Experience with Java, C, or other compiled languages Comprehensive knowledge of Saturday Night Live sketches (just kidding) Experience with SQL/NoSQL, Spark, Hadoop Familiarity with Javascript and Scripting Familiarity with Docker, GitLab, and React The total package: Our total compensation package was strategically designed with our members in mind with the intention to: reward our members for their hard work and commitment to our customers' missions; allow members to share in Red Alpha's success as we continue to grow and expand our footprint; provide long-term career opportunities through stability and internal mobility; and provide the resources our members need to support themselves and their dependents in the form of a robust benefits package. Our total compensation package includes a competitive base salary and benefits such as health, life/disability, 401k, paid time off, professional development, and generous bonus programs. Please visit our benefits tab for additional information. Salary Range: Disclosed pay ranges are a general guideline, and are not a guarantee of a final salary or compensation. Our approach in determining final salaries takes into consideration a number of factors such as education, certifications, total years of relevant professional experience, actual level of expertise, and the responsibilities of the role itself. Based on the outlined roles, responsibilities, and requirements, the projected pay range for these positions are: Entry-level: $95,000 - $135,000 Mid-level: $110,000 - $155,000 Senior-level: $135,000 - $235,000 Some of our additional perks and benefits include: Retire sooner than planned: Get closer to retirement with up to 10% in 401k contributions, immediately vested. Have a career AND a life: Enjoy up to 5 weeks of leave (25 days of personal time off) and 11 paid floating holidays. Stay at your best: As a member, we'll pay 100% of your premiums for comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance. We'll also pay the majority of the premiums for your family. Let's not forge free access to a fully equipped state of the art gym! Keep current on new technologies and technological advancements: $5250 per year towards ongoing education, trainings, certifications, and maintaining professional memberships. Dress in style: Spend up to $300 per year on company branded merchandise featuring top quality brands such as Under Armour, Nike, Carhartt, YETI, etc. Enjoy the culture: Attend fun company events throughout the year such as our Oktoberfest, summer picnic, and annual holiday party! These are all in additon to your team events which may include happy hours, baseball games, snowboarding, RenFest, and more! Every day, our elite customers are pushing through "the grind" to defeat the enemy, even putting their lives on the line for our freedom.
